sentences.text: This dinosaur possessed a slender, flat snout that was extremely elongated.
The animal had long forelimbs that ended in very long and thin hands with three fingers.
The snout was so long it measured 25% more than the length of its femur.
Unlike most relatives where the second finger was significantly longer, these three fingers were proportionally shorter and essentially equal in length.
It had a very elongated body with a shallow chest and hind legs adapted for running that ended in a retractable claw.
Estimates suggest the creature reached a length of 1.20 meters, a height of 40 centimeters, and a weight of 5 kilograms.
The fossils were found at a site named La Buitrera, which translates to vulture roost.
The genus name Buitreraptor means vulture raider, combining the Spanish word for vulture and the Latin word for seizer.
Because its teeth lacked serrations and functioned only to hold food, the animal likely swallowed prey whole.
The dinosaur Buitreraptor was first described in 2005, with Buitreraptor gonzalezorum as its type species.
Four specimens of Buitreraptor were discovered in 2004 in Patagonia, Argentina, during an excavation led by Sebastián Apesteguia and Peter Makovicky.
Four Buitreraptor skeletons were found between 2001 and 2004 in the Candeleros Formation, dating to approximately 94 million years ago.
The holotype specimen MPCA 245 is a nearly complete articulated adult skeleton housed at the Museo Provincial Carlos Ameghino in Cipolletti, Argentina.
Buitreraptor gonzalezorum is the only known species within the genus Buitreraptor.
The specific name gonzalezorum honors the González brothers, Fabian and Jorge, who performed much of the excavation and preparation work.
Scientists concluded that Buitreraptor hunted small animals like lizards and mammals rather than large prey.
Unenlagiines, including Buitreraptor, were better adapted for running and pursuit predation than the stockier Laurasian dromaeosaurids.
Although no feathers have been found on Buitreraptor fossils, it is likely the dinosaur was feathered based on evidence from its close relatives.
Initial researchers concluded that Buitreraptor hunted small animals like lizards and mammals rather than large prey like some other dromaeosaurids.
Buitreraptor was assigned to the family Dromaeosauridae and the subfamily Unenlagiinae in 2005.
Buitreraptor exhibits a mosaic of traits found in dromaeosaurids, troodontids, and avialans.
Buitreraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) in Argentina within the Candeleros Formation.
Buitreraptor lived at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 92 to 95 million years ago, in what is now South America.
Buitreraptor lived approximately 94 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range for Buitreraptor as the Albian stage, from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
An alternative hypothesis suggests dromaeosaurids originated in Laurasia and migrated to Gondwana during the Cretaceous, as southern species possess distinct traits not shared by northern relatives.
